hero.headline: US stocks post worst day of 2026 as tech selloff deepens and rate fears mount
hero.body:
The US stock market suffered its steepest decline of the year on Friday, with the S&P 500 falling more than 2.6 percent and the Nasdaq plunging 4 percent in its worst single-day drop since April 2025. The sharp selloff ended a nine-week winning streak for major indexes and wiped out recent gains as investors fled technology stocks and recalibrated their expectations for interest rates.

The market turbulence followed a stronger-than-expected jobs report showing US employers added 172,000 positions in May, sustaining a vigorous pace of hiring that has persisted through recent economic shocks. The robust employment figures reinforced trader concerns that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates to prevent the economy from overheating, with betting markets now pricing in higher odds of a Fed rate hike in coming months.

Technology stocks bore the brunt of the selling pressure, with chip manufacturers and artificial intelligence companies leading the decline. Broadcom and Intel shares dropped sharply, while other semiconductor stocks including Super Micro and Qualcomm also tumbled. The tech-heavy Nasdaq saw its biggest daily percentage fall since early 2025, reflecting growing nervousness about stretched valuations in the sector that has powered much of the market's recent rally.

Beyond equities, the selloff rippled through other asset classes. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since the November 2024 election, sinking to its lowest level since October 2024 as investors rotated away from speculative assets. The cryptocurrency's decline marked a sharp reversal from its earlier strength following the election outcome.

The market retreat highlighted tensions between strong economic data and investor preferences for lower interest rates. While the May employment report demonstrated the job market's resilience in pushing past recent strains, wage growth has not kept pace with higher prices, and consumer sentiment remains pessimistic. The Federal Reserve now faces renewed pressure to balance supporting growth against the risk of persistent inflation, a calculation that could shape monetary policy decisions in the months ahead and determine whether the market's extended rally can resume.

cards.headline: Iran strikes US military in Kuwait as regional tensions escalate
cards.body:
Iran launched a drone attack on Kuwait International Airport that killed multiple people and injured others, according to reports from multiple news outlets. The strike targeted US military personnel stationed at the airport, marking a direct escalation in hostilities between Iran and American forces in the region.

Kuwait released surveillance video showing the moment of the attack. The drone strike occurred amid ongoing tensions between the United States and Iran, following earlier confrontations in the region. The attack on Kuwaiti soil represents a significant expansion of the conflict, drawing a third country into direct involvement.

The strike on Kuwait came as Israel and Lebanon agreed to renew their ceasefire. The timing of the Iranian attack suggests a broader pattern of regional instability, with multiple flash points active simultaneously across the Middle East. The attack has disrupted travel throughout the region, adding to existing security concerns at airports and transportation hubs.

Kuwait hosts US military forces as part of longstanding defense agreements between the two countries. The presence of American troops in Kuwait dates back decades and serves as a strategic position for US operations in the Middle East. The airport strike puts Kuwaiti infrastructure and civilians at risk while targeting American military personnel.

The attack represents one of the most direct strikes by Iran against US forces in recent months. Previous confrontations have typically occurred in international waters or through proxy forces in other countries. The decision to strike US military targets in Kuwait signals an escalation in Iranian willingness to engage American forces directly, raising concerns about further military action in the region.

cards.headline: CDC warns Ebola outbreak could infect 20,000 without immediate action
cards.body:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention released modeling showing that an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could sicken more than 20,000 people in the next three months without swift intervention. Health officials stress that immediate action is needed to prevent the outbreak from matching the scale of previous major epidemics.

The outbreak, identified in mid-May in the DRC, involves the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. As of the latest reports, the virus has caused 344 confirmed cases and 60 deaths in the DRC, with 15 confirmed cases including one death in neighboring Uganda. However, the World Health Organization head Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus indicated the outbreak may have started much earlier than May. "It could be January, it could be February, March, April," he said, noting that the virus has had "a big head start." The first identified case involved a nurse who visited a health center on April 24.

Response efforts face significant obstacles. Contact tracing, a crucial element of controlling any infectious disease outbreak, remains a major challenge. Currently, only about 45 percent of contacts are being followed up, and Tedros said the number needs to exceed 90 percent to get ahead of the outbreak. Insecurity and population displacement in Ituri province, the most affected region, are hampering these efforts.

Community mistrust is another barrier to containment. Tedros reported that some community leaders in the DRC do not believe Ebola is real and worry that response measures will divert resources from other essential services. Additionally, blanket travel restrictions imposed by countries including the United States are disrupting supply chains and hindering the response, according to WHO officials.

Despite these challenges, there are signs of progress. Treatment centers have been established across Ituri province. Laboratory and diagnostic capacity is being scaled up in affected areas and neighboring regions. The number of suspected cases fell significantly when officials worked through a testing backlog, dropping from over 1,000 to 116 as cases were either confirmed or ruled out.

There is currently no vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain. However, Tedros highlighted an important development: six people in the DRC and two in Uganda have recovered from the virus, showing that survival is possible when patients receive proper care and seek treatment early.

Health officials have emphasized that early investment in outbreak response costs far less than managing a full-scale epidemic. The CDC's three-month projection window suggests there is still an opportunity to prevent escalation, but officials warn that the window for action is closing rapidly. The response is catching up to the outbreak, but swift international coordination and increased resources remain critical.

cards.headline: Senate passes immigration enforcement package after 18-hour voting session
cards.body:
The Senate concluded an 18-hour voting marathon to pass an immigration enforcement package, ending a contentious legislative battle that tested the chamber's endurance and political divisions. The extended session, known as a vote-a-rama, required senators to cast dozens of votes on amendments and final passage of the legislation.

The immigration enforcement package represents a significant legislative achievement for Republicans pushing stricter border security measures. The vote-a-rama process allowed unlimited amendments, forcing senators to take positions on a wide range of immigration-related issues throughout the night and into the following day.

The lengthy session highlighted deep partisan divisions over immigration policy. Senators debated measures ranging from border wall funding to detention policies and asylum procedures. The process tested the physical stamina of lawmakers, many of whom remained on the Senate floor throughout the night to participate in successive votes.

The package now moves to implementation, though its passage through the Senate does not guarantee immediate policy changes. The legislation's specific provisions and their practical effects on border enforcement will depend on how federal agencies interpret and apply the new authorities granted by Congress.

The vote-a-rama concluded what Senate leaders described as one of the most demanding legislative sessions in recent memory. The extended voting period allowed both parties to force votes on politically sensitive amendments, creating a record that will likely feature in upcoming election campaigns. The final tally showed party-line divisions on most major provisions, reflecting the ongoing national debate over immigration policy and border security.

cards.headline: Putin rejects Zelenskyy proposal for direct peace talks
cards.teaser: The Russian president said meeting with his Ukrainian counterpart would serve no purpose in ending the war.
cards.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has rejected Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's proposal for face-to-face peace talks. Speaking at the St Petersburg economic forum, Putin described Zelenskyy's open letter as rude and said he sees no point in meeting with him, refusing even to use Zelenskyy's name.

Instead of pursuing negotiations, Putin reaffirmed Russia's war objectives in Ukraine, including the seizure of the entire eastern Donbas region. He instructed the Russian army to continue its operations.

cards.headline: US employers add 172,000 jobs in May as labor market defies slowdown
cards.teaser: Payrolls rose more than economists expected, with unemployment at 4.3 percent, though wage growth lags rising prices.
cards.body:
US employers added 172,000 jobs in May, with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.3%. The hiring gains marked the third consecutive month of job growth, demonstrating labor market resilience despite rising inflation and Middle East tensions. Many of the new positions were in restaurants, bars, and hotels.

While employment remained strong, wage growth slowed and failed to keep pace with inflation, leaving consumers pessimistic about economic conditions. The robust jobs data also roiled financial markets, with the Nasdaq dropping 4% on Friday—its largest single-day decline in over a year—as investors worried about potential interest rate increases.

cards.headline: Trump administration discusses possible government stake in OpenAI
cards.teaser: The president plans to meet with artificial intelligence company leaders about US investment arrangements.
cards.body:
President Trump is scheduled to meet with leaders from artificial intelligence companies as soon as next week to discuss a potential government profit-sharing plan. The Trump administration has been in discussions with OpenAI about a possible government stake in the AI startup.

The meetings will focus on US investment in AI companies and how the government might participate in their growth. The proposal has drawn varied reactions, with some commentators describing the approach as a step toward AI state socialism, while others have suggested that artificial intelligence represents a public resource that should benefit citizens directly.

cards.headline: France opens investigation into Israeli treatment of flotilla activists
cards.teaser: Activists detained while trying to reach Gaza said they were abused in Israeli custody.
cards.body:
France has opened an investigation into how Israeli authorities treated activists detained aboard a flotilla heading toward Gaza. The activists have alleged they experienced abuse while in Israeli custody. Israeli authorities have disputed these claims of mistreatment.

The flotilla was intercepted before reaching Gaza, and those aboard were detained by Israeli forces. France's decision to investigate indicates the case involves French nationals or circumstances within French jurisdiction.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to ISS after air leak forces shelter procedure
cards.teaser: Five astronauts took shelter during a Russian repair attempt on a leaking tunnel section of the space station.
cards.body:
NASA ordered five astronauts aboard the International Space Station to prepare for possible evacuation after Russian specialists detected two air leaks. The leaks were discovered while pressurizing the transfer chamber of the Zveda module during routine maintenance operations.

After the repair work was paused, NASA gave the astronauts clearance to return to normal operations. The crew has since resumed their regular positions aboard the station.

cards.headline: EU says Montenegro could join by 2028 after Balkans summit
cards.teaser: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is within reach of membership in two years.
cards.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is "within reach" of joining the European Union by 2028 following a summit on Balkan expansion. EU leaders expressed optimism about rapidly expanding membership in the region.

Germany and France proposed plans to accelerate benefits for EU candidate countries in the Balkans and Moldova. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced the EU would move forward with integrating Western Balkan nations. The push for expansion aims to counter growing Russian and Chinese influence in the region.

cards.headline: Sikhs in Southampton stay home after murder sparks tensions
cards.teaser: Community members said they were scared to leave their houses following the killing of Henry Nowak.
cards.body:
Sikhs in Southampton said they were frightened to go out after the murder of Henry Nowak by Vickrum Digwa. A local gurdwara reported being empty as community members stayed home. Sikh MPs stated the murder was not about their religion.

The killing brought sudden tensions to Britain's Sikh community. Henry Nowak's father spoke publicly about the case, and a Sikh MP wrote about why everyone should pay attention to his words. The incident has shaken the community despite assurances from Sikh political leaders that the crime was not religiously motivated.

cards.headline: Everest guide found alive after six days on mountain
cards.teaser: Dawa Sherpa survived by eating chocolate and chewing ice while stranded on the world's tallest peak.
cards.body:
Dawa Sherpa, a 57-year-old mountain guide, was discovered alive on Mount Everest nearly a week after going missing. A cleaning crew spotted him sliding down the mountain and helped with his rescue. He survived the ordeal by eating chocolate and chewing ice during his time alone at extreme altitude.

After his rescue, Sherpa spoke to reporters from a hospital bed. His wife expressed concern that more could have been done to locate him sooner, suggesting the search effort could have been more thorough. His survival for six days at high elevation is remarkable, as conditions on Everest typically become fatal within hours.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors pursue multiple election fraud investigations
cards.teaser: The Justice Department confirmed it is conducting several investigations into alleged election fraud, with one prosecutor sent to observe ballot counting in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
A top federal prosecutor confirmed that the Justice Department is pursuing multiple election fraud investigations across the country. The announcement came as President Trump made claims without evidence that Democrats were attempting to steal California primary elections.

The DOJ sent a prosecutor to observe ballot counting in Los Angeles amid the allegations. California officials pushed back against the federal probe, with state leaders clashing with the Trump administration over what they characterized as baseless accusations of cheating in the primary process.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to International Space Station after air leak repair attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts returned to normal operations after sheltering during a Russian effort to repair an air leak in a tunnel area of the station.
cards.body:
Astronauts aboard the International Space Station have resumed normal duties after being placed on evacuation alert due to air leaks discovered in the Zveda module's transfer chamber. NASA ordered the crew to enter their docked Crew Dragon spacecraft and don spacesuits as a precautionary measure while Russian specialists investigated the leaks.

The air leaks were detected during pressurization of the transfer chamber. After Russian operations teams assessed the situation, NASA cleared the crew to return to regular operations on the station.

cards.headline: FAA says Trump arch near Arlington will require red warning lights
cards.teaser: Federal aviation officials ruled that a proposed arch near Arlington National Cemetery must have red lights for aircraft safety, as the project clears another regulatory hurdle.
cards.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration determined that the proposed Trump arch near Arlington National Cemetery will need red warning lights for aviation safety. The decision came as the project cleared another regulatory hurdle despite concerns about sightlines and views in the area.

Washington planning officials argued that the arch would not be subject to the law limiting building height in the District of Columbia. Critics have said adding the structure would obstruct views of existing monuments and landmarks in the capital area.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate denies allegations of physically rough behavior
cards.teaser: Graham Platner denied accusations from former girlfriends of unsettling and physically rough behavior, calling the reports a sign his campaign is gaining momentum.
cards.body:
Graham Platner is denying accusations that he was physically rough with former girlfriends, following a New York Times report in which several women described unsettling behavior during their relationships with him.

Platner's campaign has faced multiple controversies in recent weeks. Despite the allegations and other issues, Maine Democrats have indicated they will continue supporting his Senate candidacy, and Platner himself views the controversies as signs his campaign is gaining traction.

cards.headline: Visitors say repainted Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool looks unchanged
cards.teaser: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is being refilled after President Trump had it painted in a shade he called American flag blue, but visitors say the results are subtle.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is being refilled following a repainting project ordered by President Trump. Workers painted the pool bottom in a color called "American flag blue," a costly undertaking that has now been completed.

Visitors to the site have noted that the results appear subtle, with many questioning what has visibly changed. Some observers described the finished product as looking black rather than notably blue, raising questions about the impact of the expensive renovation project.

cards.headline: Murder trial continues for teen accused of fatal stabbing at Texas track meet
cards.teaser: Jurors in the Karmelo Anthony trial watched video of Austin Metcalf's death and the suspect's arrest as the case over a fatal stabbing at a Frisco ISD track meet enters its fourth day.
cards.body:
The murder trial of Karmelo Anthony continued with emotional testimony and video evidence shown to jurors. Anthony is accused of fatally stabbing Austin Metcalf at a Frisco Independent School District track meet. Teen witnesses described the confrontation that led to the death.

A witness testified that Anthony had been asked to leave opposing teams' areas 15 times before the fatal stabbing occurred. Jurors viewed video footage of both Metcalf's death and Anthony's subsequent arrest. The trial is taking place in Texas and has drawn significant local attention.

cards.headline: Google signs $920 million monthly deal with SpaceX for computing capacity
cards.teaser: Google will pay SpaceX nearly $1 billion per month for compute capacity in a major cloud computing agreement.
cards.body:
Google reached an agreement to pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity at xAI data centers. According to Google, the deal stems from unexpected demand for its recently launched AI products.

The arrangement represents a major recurring revenue stream for SpaceX as it diversifies beyond its core rocket launch and satellite internet businesses. The deal comes as SpaceX prepares for a potential initial public offering.

cards.headline: US states prepare lawsuit to block Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros
cards.teaser: Multiple state attorneys general are developing legal action to challenge the proposed merger between the two major entertainment companies.
cards.body:
A coalition of US states is preparing a lawsuit aimed at blocking Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros, according to sources familiar with the matter. The legal challenge represents the latest hurdle for a deal that has faced criticism from various quarters since its announcement.

Paramount's top lawyer responded to critics of the merger, stating that some opposition to the Warner Bros deal stems from antisemitic motivations. The company's general counsel also criticized what he described as fear-mongering and partisan politics clouding debate over the transaction. Bloomberg reported that Paramount wants a separate lawsuit seeking to block the deal dismissed.

cards.headline: Bitcoin drops below $60,000 for first time since 2024 election
cards.teaser: The cryptocurrency fell to its lowest level since October 2024 as investors shifted focus to artificial intelligence and other assets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday, reaching its lowest point since October 2024. This marks the first time the cryptocurrency has traded beneath that level since November's presidential election.

The decline reflects shifting investor priorities, with capital moving toward artificial intelligence stocks and major technology companies. The price weakness has sparked debate among analysts about what the drop signals for cryptocurrency's future trajectory.

cards.headline: Chip stocks extend selloff as Broadcom and Intel shares tumble
cards.teaser: Semiconductor manufacturers led market declines after Broadcom earnings disappointed investors.
cards.body:
Broadcom and Intel shares dropped sharply on Friday as the selloff in chip stocks intensified. The decline followed disappointing earnings from Broadcom, which failed to meet investor expectations and triggered broader concerns about the semiconductor sector.

Other technology stocks also suffered significant losses, with Super Micro and Qualcomm among those getting hit hard. The chip selloff contributed to the Nasdaq's worst single-day performance of the year, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average managed to jump as traders explored opportunities in non-technology sectors.

hero.headline: Astronauts shelter in safe area as Russian crew attempts to repair air leak on space station
hero.body:
Five astronauts aboard the International Space Station sheltered in their spacecraft Friday as Russian crew members attempted repairs on persistent air leaks in the station's Russian segment. The precaution was lifted after about two hours when repair efforts were paused for further assessment.

NASA ordered the crew to take shelter in the Dragon spacecraft and prepare for possible evacuation while Roscosmos worked on the leaks. The five astronauts included four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission: American astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, French astronaut Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency, and Russian cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev. American astronaut Chris Williams, who has been aboard the station for 190 days, also sheltered in place alongside Russian cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergey Mikayev.

The air leaks were discovered in the transfer tunnel of the Zvezda Service Module during pressurization procedures. Russian specialists detected two leak sites and successfully sealed one using a two-component sealant called Germetal-1. The second potential leak was located on the conical portion of the transfer chamber. Roscosmos stated that neither the crew nor the station's onboard systems faced immediate danger.

After the repair work was paused for additional measurements and data analysis, NASA instructed the crew to end their safe haven procedures and return to normal station operations. "Roscosmos has paused Friday's structural repair efforts inside the Zvezda service module transfer tunnel as more measurements and data is assessed," said Bethany Stevens, a NASA spokesperson. "Given this development, NASA has instructed the crew members inside the Dragon spacecraft to end the safe haven procedures and return to planned operations aboard the International Space Station. We look forward to working with Roscosmos on a collaborative approach to address the leaks."

The air leak problem represents an ongoing concern for the aging orbital laboratory. Roscosmos has been dealing with cracks and air leaks in its station compartments for more than five years, with NASA's office of inspector general identifying them as a top safety risk. In June, a chartered spaceflight carrying India, Poland, and Hungary's first astronauts in decades was postponed due to leak concerns.

The Zvezda Service Module, where the leaks occurred, is approximately 43 feet long and contains living quarters, life support systems, communications equipment, electrical power distribution, data processing systems, flight control systems, and propulsion systems. It was the first fully Russian contribution to the ISS and includes a docking port for Russian Soyuz and Progress spacecraft.

The International Space Station has maintained continuous human presence for 25 years and is operated by five partner space agencies: NASA, the Canadian Space Agency, the European Space Agency, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, and Roscosmos.

cards.headline: Google agrees to pay SpaceX $920 million monthly for computing capacity
cards.teaser: The tech giant described the arrangement as a response to unexpected demand for its AI products.
cards.body:
Google has reached an agreement with SpaceX to pay the space and telecommunications company $920 million per month for computing capacity. The deal represents a significant financial commitment between the two companies.

A Google representative said the agreement resulted from unexpected demand for the company's recently launched artificial intelligence products. The computing arrangement will provide Google with additional capacity to support its expanding AI operations.

cards.headline: Former IBM cybersecurity executive files lawsuit alleging company covered up data breaches
cards.teaser: The whistleblower lawsuit accuses IBM and two subsidiaries of not disclosing breaches during the mid-2010s.
cards.body:
A former cybersecurity executive has filed a lawsuit against IBM, claiming the company concealed multiple data breaches that occurred in the mid-2010s. According to the complaint, IBM and two subsidiary companies were breached but failed to publicly disclose the incidents.

The whistleblower alleges that IBM deliberately covered up the breaches rather than reporting them transparently.

cards.headline: Small modular nuclear reactor achieves criticality in startup's first test
cards.teaser: The reactor from Antares marks a milestone but is not yet ready to generate power.
cards.body:
A small modular nuclear reactor developed by startup company Antares has reached criticality in its first test. Criticality occurs when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining chain reaction, representing a key milestone in reactor development.

The reactor is not yet ready to generate power for commercial use. Small modular reactors are designed to be smaller and more flexible than traditional nuclear power plants, with proponents arguing they could provide carbon-free energy more efficiently and at lower cost than conventional reactors.

cards.headline: S&P 500 denies SpaceX entry to index, blocking OpenAI and Anthropic as well
cards.teaser: The decision prevents the companies from accessing billions of dollars from passive investors.
cards.body:
SpaceX has been rejected from entry into the S&P 500 index, a decision that also blocks other private companies including OpenAI and Anthropic from joining. The rejection means these companies will not gain access to the investment flows that come with index inclusion.

Inclusion in the S&P 500 typically opens companies to billions of dollars from passive investors who track the index through mutual funds and exchange-traded funds. The rejection keeps these prominent private companies outside the reach of this significant pool of institutional investment capital.

cards.headline: Popular speaker model can be remotely hacked to infect other connected devices
cards.teaser: The manufacturer does not consider the security issue a vulnerability.
cards.body:
Security researchers have found that the Sound Blaster Katana V2X speaker can be hacked over the air, potentially allowing attackers to infect other devices connected to the same network. The speaker has received positive reviews from consumers.

The seller of the Sound Blaster Katana V2X does not consider the behavior a vulnerability. This position suggests the company may not issue a patch or security update to address the issue, leaving users potentially exposed to the remote hacking risk.

cards.headline: Data center developer cuts project size by half following community opposition
cards.teaser: The company said it felt it had no choice but to shrink the facility amid protests.
cards.body:
A developer has reduced the size of a planned data center by 50 percent after facing protests from the surrounding community. The company acknowledged it angered many people with the original proposal.

A representative for the developer said the company felt beaten up by the opposition and had no choice but to shrink the data center plans. The reduction represents a significant scaling back of the original facility design in response to local concerns.

hero.headline: Ned Jarrett, Two-Time NASCAR Champion and Hall of Fame Announcer, Dies at 93
hero.body:
Ned Jarrett, a legendary figure in NASCAR history, has died at age 93. The racing icon earned recognition both as a champion driver and as a respected broadcast announcer across a career spanning several decades.

Jarrett secured NASCAR Cup Series championships in 1961 and 1965, establishing himself as a dominant force during the sport's early years. He competed during a formative period when stock car racing was building its reputation as a major American sport. His driving success and professional approach helped lay the groundwork for NASCAR's growth and wider appeal.

Following his retirement from competition, Jarrett transitioned into broadcasting, where his career proved equally successful. Known for his distinctive voice and insightful analysis, he became one of the sport's most celebrated commentators.

Jarrett's most iconic broadcasting moment occurred at the 1993 Daytona 500, when his son Dale Jarrett was competing in the closing laps of the race. The emotional call captured Jarrett encouraging his son toward victory, including direction to take the high side of the track. This broadcast moment became one of the most memorable and frequently replayed calls in NASCAR history. It exemplified both the sport's family traditions and the genuine emotion that made Jarrett an effective communicator with viewers. Broadcaster Mike Joy later discussed behind-the-scenes aspects of that famous call, highlighting how Jarrett maintained his professionalism while watching his son race for one of motorsports' most prestigious victories.

The NASCAR Hall of Fame inducted Jarrett, recognizing his substantial contributions to the sport. Beyond his personal accomplishments, he played a mentoring role for younger drivers and broadcasters throughout his later years. The Jarrett family name remains prominent in NASCAR circles through his son Dale, who also achieved success as a championship-caliber driver. Ned's influence continues to shape how racing is presented and consumed by fans across the sport.

Jarrett's passing represents the loss of one of NASCAR's most important figures from its foundational era. His ability to excel both as a competitor and as a storyteller made him a unique presence in motorsports history. The impact of his work in building the sport's audience and appeal continues to influence NASCAR today. His legacy encompasses not only his on-track achievements and announcing career but also his role in advancing the sport's popularity and helping establish NASCAR as a cultural institution in America.

cards.headline: Yankees Star Aaron Judge Out 4-6 Weeks With Rib Stress Fracture
cards.teaser: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge was diagnosed with a rib stress fracture and will be reevaluated in four to six weeks.
cards.body:
The Yankees announced that Judge has a stress fracture in his rib, sidelining one of baseball's premier sluggers for at least a month during the heart of the season. Judge addressed the injury and discussed his expected return timeline, explaining how he sustained the fracture.

With Judge out, the Yankees called up prospect Spencer Jones to fill the roster spot. The injury has significant implications for New York's playoff positioning and could influence the team's strategy at the upcoming trade deadline. Fantasy baseball managers are scrambling to find replacement options for Judge, one of the game's most productive hitters.

cards.headline: Matteo Arnaldi Withdraws From French Open Semifinal With Illness
cards.teaser: Italian player Matteo Arnaldi pulled out of his French Open semifinal against Flavio Cobolli after spending the night vomiting due to a virus.
cards.body: Flavio Cobolli advanced to the French Open final without playing after Matteo Arnaldi withdrew from their semifinal due to a virus. Cobolli will face Alexander Zverev in the championship match after Zverev defeated Jakub Mensik in four sets to reach his first Grand Slam final.

cards.headline: Browns Trade Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and Three Draft Picks
cards.teaser: Cleveland sent defensive star Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks, including a first-rounder.
cards.body:
The trade gives Cleveland another first-round selection for the 2027 NFL Draft as the franchise reshapes its roster. Garrett, one of the league's premier pass rushers, heads to Los Angeles where the Rams continue adding talent despite their aggressive trading history.

CBS Sports ranked the Garrett deal among their favorite trades of the 2026 offseason. The move has major implications for both teams' defensive units, with the Rams strengthening their pass rush while Cleveland accumulates draft capital for a rebuild. Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim reacted to speculation that she influenced Garrett's trade decision through social media.

cards.headline: Jonny Bairstow Powers Yorkshire to Record 106-Run Victory Over Lancashire
cards.teaser: Yorkshire crushed Lancashire Lightning by 106 runs in T20 Blast action, with Jonny Bairstow and Moeen Ali leading the dominant performance.
cards.body:
Jonny Bairstow led Yorkshire to a dominant 106-run victory over Lancashire Lightning in Friday's T20 Blast clash. The commanding performance in the Roses rivalry match represented a record win for Yorkshire against their traditional rivals.

Moeen Ali also played a key role in the victory, contributing to a strong all-around team effort that stood out among the evening's T20 Blast fixtures.

cards.headline: Warrington Moves Level With Leeds After Beating Hull FC
cards.teaser: Josh Smith scored two second-half tries as Warrington defeated Hull FC to draw level on points with Leeds at the top of the Super League table.
cards.body:
Josh Smith's two second-half tries proved the difference as Warrington edged past Hull FC in a hard-fought contest. The victory moves the Wire level on points with Leeds at the top of the Super League table.

Despite a struggle at times during the match, Warrington secured the result needed to maintain their position in the title race as the season progresses.

cards.headline: Blackburn Rovers Reappoint Tony Mowbray as Head Coach
cards.teaser: Tony Mowbray returns to Blackburn Rovers for a second stint as head coach after previously managing the club.
cards.body:
Blackburn announced Mowbray's appointment, bringing back a familiar face to lead the team. Mowbray previously managed the club and now returns to take charge once again in hopes of improving Blackburn's fortunes.

The reappointment represents Blackburn's effort to find stability and success under a manager who knows the club well. Mowbray's previous experience with the Rovers is expected to help him navigate the challenges ahead as he begins his second tenure in charge.

hero.headline: Anthony Head, British actor known for Buffy and Ted Lasso, dies at 72
hero.body:
British actor Anthony Head has died at age 72 from complications related to pneumonia. His daughters Emily and Daisy announced his passing in a statement, saying he "passed away peacefully of complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family."

Head achieved worldwide recognition for his role as Rupert Giles in the supernatural drama series Buffy the Vampire Slayer. Playing the school librarian and mentor figure to Sarah Michelle Gellar's title character, he became a defining presence throughout the show's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute on Instagram, referencing her character's famous line: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok," before adding, "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

Beyond Buffy, Head demonstrated his versatility across multiple entertainment formats. He appeared in the BBC sketch comedy show Little Britain as a prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant played by David Walliams. He also took roles in the BBC fantasy series Merlin and appeared in films including The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie. More recently, he played Rupert Mannion, a former football club owner, in the Apple TV Plus comedy Ted Lasso, where he earned praise for his on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

Head's connection to entertainment began early. Born in Camden, London, he was raised by artistic parents. His father was a documentary filmmaker who founded Verity Films, while his mother was an actress who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother also pursued acting.

He began his professional career on the British stage, starring in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell. Throughout the 1980s, he appeared in various productions including the 1981 adaptation of Lady Chatterley's Lover and the 1987 film A Prayer for the Dying alongside Bob Hoskins and Liam Neeson. He took a lead role as Freddie Trumper in the original West End production of the musical Chess in 1988 and played Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

Head was also recognizable to British audiences for his iconic role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements that aired throughout the 1980s, which featured a slow-burn courtship between a British couple.

During Buffy's production, Head lived in Los Angeles while his partner Sarah and two young daughters remained in England. He told the Guardian he would travel home every three or four weeks whenever the production schedule allowed.

His daughters expressed that "our grief is far greater than the hole he has left behind but we know his legacy will live on in the shows he was a part of and in the audiences that love them."

cards.headline: New Scary Movie sets franchise opening record with $52 million
cards.teaser: The horror parody film earned the highest opening weekend in the franchise's history.
cards.body:
The latest Scary Movie installment dominated the box office with a franchise-record $52 million opening weekend. The sixth film in the series revived the parody franchise with a self-titled release, following the strategy of the original 2000 film.

Masters of the Universe opened in second place, earning over $31 million. Critics gave Scary Movie mixed reviews, noting that successful jokes were sparse in the horror spoof, which targeted everything from Scream to recent horror trends.

cards.headline: Reed Hastings exits Netflix board after 25 years as CEO
cards.teaser: The Netflix co-founder officially departed the board following the company's annual shareholders meeting.
cards.body:
Reed Hastings left the Netflix board following the company's annual shareholders meeting on June 4. Hastings co-founded Netflix and served as CEO for 25 years, leading the company's transformation into the world's leading premium streaming service.

Hastings had previously stepped down from the CEO role to become executive chairman. Jay Hoag will take over as chairman of the board. Netflix confirmed Hastings's departure was part of a previously announced transition plan.

cards.headline: Paramount announces Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin game
cards.teaser: The game marks the first project from the combined Paramount-Skydance in-house studio.
cards.body:
Paramount Games Studio revealed Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin at Summer Game Fest. The game represents the first project from the combined Paramount-Skydance in-house studios.

Platinum Games is developing the title, which Paramount Games Studio will publish. The company described The Last Ronin as a AAA action-adventure game based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise.

cards.headline: Capcom sets 2027 release for Resident Evil: Veronica remake
cards.teaser: The remake updates the 2000 game Code: Veronica for modern platforms.
cards.body:
Capcom announced Resident Evil: Veronica will release in 2027. The game remakes the 2000 title Resident Evil Code: Veronica for contemporary gaming systems.

The original Code: Veronica took place three months after the events of Resident Evil 2 and ran concurrently with Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. The story follows Claire Redfield and other characters from the franchise.

cards.headline: Avatar: Fire and Ash and Hoppers join Disney Plus in June
cards.teaser: The streaming service adds two major theatrical releases to its library this month.
cards.body:
Disney Plus will stream Avatar: Fire and Ash and Hoppers in June following their theatrical runs. James Cameron directed Fire and Ash, the latest installment in the Avatar franchise, while Pixar produced the animated film Hoppers.

Fire and Ash expands the universe of Pandora after Avatar and Avatar: The Way of Water, two of the highest-grossing films in cinema history. Both films performed successfully in theaters before moving to the streaming platform.

cards.headline: Lisa Kudrow and Michael Patrick King discuss ending The Comeback
cards.teaser: The creators spoke about concluding the HBO comedy series and its evolution over time.
cards.body:
Lisa Kudrow and Michael Patrick King addressed the conclusion of their HBO comedy The Comeback. The series has returned every ten years throughout its run, making the title more appropriate than the creators initially intended.

Kudrow and King discussed the evolution of Valerie Cherish, the show's main character, and touched on topics including artificial intelligence in entertainment. The Comeback aired on HBO over multiple limited runs spanning two decades.

hero.headline: Senate passes immigration enforcement package after 18-hour voting session
hero.body:
The Senate concluded an 18-hour voting marathon to pass an immigration enforcement package, ending a contentious legislative battle that tested the chamber's endurance and political divisions. The extended session, known as a vote-a-rama, required senators to cast dozens of votes on amendments and final passage of the legislation.

The immigration enforcement package represents a significant legislative achievement for Republicans pushing stricter border security measures. The vote-a-rama process allowed unlimited amendments, forcing senators to take positions on a wide range of immigration-related issues throughout the night and into the following day.

The lengthy session highlighted deep partisan divisions over immigration policy. Senators debated measures ranging from border wall funding to detention policies and asylum procedures. The process tested the physical stamina of lawmakers, many of whom remained on the Senate floor throughout the night to participate in successive votes.

The package now moves to implementation, though its passage through the Senate does not guarantee immediate policy changes. The legislation's specific provisions and their practical effects on border enforcement will depend on how federal agencies interpret and apply the new authorities granted by Congress.

The vote-a-rama concluded what Senate leaders described as one of the most demanding legislative sessions in recent memory. The extended voting period allowed both parties to force votes on politically sensitive amendments, creating a record that will likely feature in upcoming election campaigns. The final tally showed party-line divisions on most major provisions, reflecting the ongoing national debate over immigration policy and border security.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico's gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. The victory positions her for a general election campaign that could make history.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. Her primary win sets up what is expected to be a closely watched gubernatorial race with significant symbolic and political importance.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Early results from California's gubernatorial primary indicate Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading their respective party fields.
cards.body:
California voters cast ballots in the state's gubernatorial primary to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in early results as votes continue to be counted.

The counting process has drawn scrutiny, with the Justice Department sending a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles. Election delays have prompted unfounded claims of rigging from some political figures, though state officials have rejected these allegations.

cards.headline: Former Border Patrol commander attended far-right international conference
cards.teaser: Greg Bovino, a former Border Patrol commander, spoke at an international gathering that included white supremacists and neo-Nazis.
cards.body:
Greg Bovino, who previously commanded Border Patrol operations, recently participated as a speaker at an international far-right conference. The event included white supremacists and neo-Nazis among its attendees and speakers.

Bovino's appearance at the gathering raises questions about his connections to extremist movements. His role in the conference comes amid ongoing scrutiny of extremism within law enforcement and border security agencies.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats call for halt to Trump gold coin production
cards.teaser: Two Democratic senators urged the Treasury Department to stop producing commemorative gold coins bearing President Trump's image.
cards.body:
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Ron Wyden called on the Trump administration to halt production of a 24-karat gold coin featuring the president's image. The coin was designed to commemorate America's 250th birthday.

The senators raised concerns that some gold used by the U.S. Mint could be traced to foreign cartels. Their letter to the Treasury Department highlights worries about both the appropriateness of the presidential imagery and the sourcing of materials for the commemorative coins.

cards.headline: Reflecting Pool reopens after Trump-ordered repainting
cards.teaser: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is refilling after being painted in what President Trump called American flag blue.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is refilling after undergoing a repainting project ordered by President Trump. The pool was coated with a color the administration called "American flag blue."

The renovation took several weeks to complete and reportedly cost millions of dollars. However, visitors returning to see the results say the color change is subtle, with some describing the pool's appearance as darker than before. The expensive project has prompted questions about how federal funds are being allocated for aesthetic modifications to national monuments.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner denies conduct allegations
cards.teaser: Republican Senate candidate Graham Platner denied accusations of physical roughness with former girlfriends reported by The New York Times.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Maine Senate candidate, has denied accusations that he was physically rough with former girlfriends, according to a New York Times report. Platner stated he has no intention of withdrawing from the race.

Platner characterized the Times report and surrounding controversies as signs that his campaign is gaining momentum. The Maine Senate race has drawn increased national attention and scrutiny of candidates.
